lines.text: Here's why long Claude Code sessions got cheaper, in under sixty seconds.
Say you ask Claude Code to fix a bug.
Every turn, it re-sends the whole conversation in tokens, small pieces of words, including your ask, the files it read, and every tool result.
For every token Claude writes, it now reads three hundred twenty-four, up from one hundred eighty-nine in March.
Reading a cached token, one saved from an earlier turn, is now sixty percent cheaper.
Claude Code also breaks the cache less often. Refreshing your login or adding instructions mid-conversation are less likely to reset it, so input that misses the cache fell by more than half.
And Opus five point five needs fewer turns for the same job. Together, that's an estimated forty percent cheaper than Opus five.
Run slash usage to see how much of yours is cached reads, because no single number holds for every codebase.
